R6E-deer-drive-0001.name: 1.2 km NE of Bish Creek
R6E-deer-drive-0001.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a town (estimate).
R6E-deer-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: No official deer winter range within 500 m, so the top score here is 8 of 11. This score leans on cutblocks, burns, habitat zone and aspect.
Cutblock harvested 2007 (19 years old), right here.
Burn from 2016 (fire R50087, 13 ha), 700 m S.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHvm3): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SW facing slope, 11 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from District of Kitimat, about 4 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.96366, -128.78486, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 40 m NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 8 m, about 5 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2007 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-11, Region 6. Season: mule deer bucks Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 50, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-16, closures 2026-10-16.
R6E-deer-drive-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-11: about 343 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.02 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: close to pavement, a town or a rec site. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.0 km and about 8 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
